title: The zodiac figure labels do not repeat as an ordered list from sign to sign, whatever the starting point
statement: If the labels beside the figures of the zodiac roundels named the degrees or days of a sign (a common reading of the thirty figures per sign), the same words would follow in the same order on every sign, up to where each ring starts. Tested on the 12 public zodiac pages (ZL, all label loci of section Z in transcription order: f70v1, f70v2, f71r, f71v, f72r1, f72r2, f72r3, f72v1, f72v2, f72v3, f73r, f73v; 17 to 41 labels each, 350 in all). For every pair of pages I counted labels equal at the same position, and then took the best of every cyclic offset of one ring against the other, so a ring transcribed from a different starting figure is matched at its best alignment. Null: each page's labels in a random order (40 draws), the same best-offset count. Same position, no offset: 0.18% of positions agree exactly, against 0.06% to 0.29% at offsets of 3, 5 or 7. Best offset per pair, summed over the 66 pairs: 41 exact agreements against a null mean of 40.1 (p = 0.34); allowing one glyph of difference, 115 against 114.0 (p = 0.41). So nothing in the order of the labels repeats from sign to sign: they are not a fixed sequence of degree or day names written out in order, whether as whole words or with one glyph changed for the sign, and the ring order is no help as an anchor. Limits: the transcription order of label loci may not follow the ring exactly on every page, and names that change by more than one glyph per sign would not be caught. Several label words do recur across signs (otaly six times on four zodiac pages, okeey, okaly, otedy), but not at corresponding places in the ring. No anchor follows from this.
check: Rerun on the public zodiac pages: same-position and best-cyclic-offset agreement of label sequences between every pair of signs, against labels shuffled within each page.
